messages:
alex: Heads-up — sketching a lightweight safefile compatibility handshake for hotload paths. TL;DR: fetch metadata header (shard sizes, comp/quant flags, codec, soft-version) synchronously, decide eligibility, then either optimistic background hydrate or fallback to compatible variant. avoid blocking full checksums during critical path.

maria: curious how this differs from the existing manifest sidecar approach? sounds like a smaller RTT but more requests?

alex: yep. current sidecar+manifest often requires reading index+footer which can be hefty. idea is metadata-first: tiny header (~1-2KB) returned from object store with compact flags. if header indicates incompatible compress/quant, we skip immediately. otherwise we try optimistic read + lazy checksum.

jon: main worry: optimistic background hydrate could still OOM if we mispredict working set. what's the eviction/guard?

alex: two mitigations: 1) a pre-allocated "prep" arena sized to n-hotstart-pages for optimistic reads; if arena exhausted, we fall back to streamed decode (higher latency but safe). 2) priority hints in header let runtime order hotstarts to avoid cross-shard bursts.

sasha: raw handshake example (proto idea):
```json
{
  "shard_id":"model-x-0003.p-12",
  "shard_size":23456789,
  "compressed":true,
  "compression":"zstd:chunked",
  "quantized":true,
  "quant_profile":"q4_0",
  "soft_version":"safefile-v2",
  "preferred_hotstart":true,
  "eviction_hint":3,
  "signature":"sig-v1:base64.."
}
```
sasha: header stays small, we can diff on soft_version to decide compatibility.

maria: sounds good. what's the perf/latency tradeoff? extra RTT for header vs pulling full footer later?

alex: measurement hypothesis: header RTT ~5-10ms on same region; avoids a full 50-150ms wasted warmup on big shard misses. net win for sub-200ms SLO apps. but needs benchmarking for cold-path vs steady-state.

lisa: security question: are you relying on the store for signature verification? want to make sure we don't accept tampered headers.

alex: we sign headers server-side; runtime verifies with KMS-backed keys. header includes signature and key-id. can also fall back to signed manifest verification if header signature absent.

jon: another edge: mixed-format bundles (some shards q4, some fp16). handshake should be able to express per-layer/segment features or "coarse-grain" only?

sasha: prefer coarse-grain in handshake to keep header tiny. for per-layer mismatch we surface an additional `detail_url` pointing at signed manifest/sidecar for out-of-band inspection. runtime can choose to lazy-validate detail if needed.

alex: implementation plan: 1) spec header fields + signature, 2) loader API changes: fast_check(header) -> enum {accept, accept_optimistic, reject}, 3) runtime resource reservation & eviction guards, 4) perf tests + canary.

maria: volunteer to run perf harness (latency/cost) across small/large shards and zstd vs raw. I'll set up test matrix. :+1:

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] canary pipeline triggered: builder/loader-handshake-proto -> staging.

sasha: I'll draft RFC follow-up w/ schema and loader interface patches. assign to @maria for perf numbers, @jon for OOM/eviction tests, @lisa for security review.

alex: awesome — feel free to ping if you want quick sync. thanks! :rocket:
